text: News Home News PROASA call with Chilean funding agency has approved proposals Versão em português Image: Copernicus Program (EU)/Wikimedia Commons Published on January 23, 2026 FAPESP and ANID have selected scientific collaborations between researchers from the state of São Paulo and Chile on topics involving coastal areas and aquatic environments of the South Atlantic and Antarctica. FAPESP announces the result of a call for proposals from its South Atlantic and Antarctica Program (PROASA), promoted in partnership with the National Agency for Research and Development (ANID) of Chile. A total of eight proposals were selected. The projects were jointly developed by two lead researchers representing, respectively, a teaching and research institution from the state of São Paulo and another from Chile. The São Paulo portion of the research will be funded by FAPESP through the Research Grant – Regular modality. The call aimed to support bilateral research on biodiversity, ocean processes, latitudinal studies, governance, and other human dimensions covering coastal areas and marine environments of the South Atlantic and Antarctica.
